claims.text: Mechanical alloying followed by spark plasma sintering will produce AlCrFeNiSi with a more compositionally homogeneous microstructure than conventional melting-based fabrication.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will produce a finer-grained AlCrFeNiSi microstructure.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will lower residual stresses in AlCrFeNiSi relative to rapid-melting or high-thermal-gradient additive manufacturing.
Mechanical alloying followed by SPS will reduce defects in AlCrFeNiSi relative to conventional rapid-melting or additive-manufacturing routes.
Mechanically alloyed AlCrFeNiSi feedstock has a relatively uniform elemental distribution on the microscale.
High-energy mechanical alloying thoroughly mixes the constituent elements of AlCrFeNiSi.
Keeping consolidation below the melting temperature avoids melt-related compositional segregation.
The proposed process will produce fully dense AlCrFeNiSi with minimal porosity.
The proposed process will reduce the population of high-angle grain boundaries.
Mechanical alloying creates an intimate and uniform distribution of alloying elements at the particle level.
Solid-state, pressure-assisted SPS avoids the high thermal gradients associated with melting-based processing.
Reduced thermal gradients and solid-state interdiffusion reduce segregation and residual thermal stress.
Reduced segregation, residual stress, and processing defects lead to improved mechanical properties.
SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi will have higher tensile strength than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
SPS-processed AlCrFeNiSi will have higher microhardness than conventionally fabricated AlCrFeNiSi.
Conventional casting or laser powder bed fusion of AlCrFeNiSi produces noticeable segregation, high residual stress, and defects such as hot cracks or porosity.
Partial melting or processing in an uncontrolled atmosphere may prevent the proposed improvements.
The exact percentage improvement in strength or hardness is not established.

The hypothesis can be tested by comparing conventionally fabricated and mechanically alloyed plus SPS samples using EDS, EBSD, XRD residual-stress measurements, tensile testing, hardness testing, and defect imaging.
Failure of the SPS samples to show statistically significant improvements in homogeneity, residual stress, and mechanical properties would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The initial state already describes the feedstock as prepared by mechanical alloying, while the intervention presents mechanical alloying as the first new processing step.
